title: The Plans Practice

header.html: Explain the purpose of the plans practice and its relationships with the principles; explain the purpose of the work package description, project product description and plans; define schedule, dependency, project plan, stage plan, team plan, exception plan and scope; describe the planning horizon, project stages, product-based planning, tolerances and delivery sustainability
the official PRINCE2 7 Foundation syllabus (PeopleCert), learning outcome 4.3

html:
1Purpose

The plans practice supports communication and control by defining the means of delivering the products: what will be delivered, how, when, by whom and at what cost. A plan is a proposal, baselined once approved.

2Plan levels

Plan Meaning
Project plan The whole project: major products, stages, overall cost, time and quality
Stage plan One management stage in detail, produced near the stage end for the next stage
Team plan The plan of a team manager for the work packages (optional)
Exception plan A plan that replaces the current plan when a tolerance would be exceeded; requested by the board

Term Meaning
Schedule The timing of activities and resources
Dependency An item or activity that must happen before another can start or finish
Scope The sum of the work (products and activities) to be done

3Planning guidance

Guidance Meaning
Planning horizon How far ahead you can plan reliably: detail near, outline far
Project stages The project is divided into management stages; detailed plan for the next stage only
Product-based planning Plan starting from the products, then the activities needed
Tolerances The permissible deviation from a plan before escalation (set for time, cost, quality, scope, benefits, risk, sustainability)
Delivery sustainability Plan so the project delivers in a sustainable way (environment, resources, social effects)

Product-based planning (the technique)

  1. Write the project product description (what the project must deliver)
  2. Create a product breakdown structure (the products as a hierarchy)
  3. Write product descriptions for the products
  4. Create a product flow diagram (the order products are built)

Then identify activities and dependencies, estimate, schedule, and assess risks. [Verify live]

Exam tip

. Product first, activities second. If an option says to list activities before knowing the products, it is not product-based planning.

4Management products

Product Purpose
Project product description What the project as a whole must deliver, with acceptance criteria
Work package description The work to be done and the product to deliver, handed from the project manager to a team manager
Plan Project, stage, team and exception plans
Exam tip

. Work package description goes to a team manager. Project product description covers the whole project. Match the product to the audience.

Exam tip

. An exception plan replaces the current plan; it is not a new, extra plan.

5Exam Q&A

5.1 Practice questions (choose the best answer)

S1A tolerance is forecast to be exceeded and the board asks for a replacement plan. Which plan is this?

  • AProject plan
  • BStage plan
  • CTeam plan
  • DException plan
Show the answer

Answer: D. An exception plan replaces the current plan when a tolerance would be exceeded.

S2Which statements about plans are CORRECT? (1) A stage plan covers one management stage. (2) A project plan covers the whole project. (3) A team plan is required for every project. (4) A dependency is an activity that can start at any time.

  • A1 and 2
  • B3 and 4
  • C2 and 3
  • D1 and 4
Show the answer

Answer: A. Stage and project plans are defined that way.

S3Identify the missing word. [ ? ] planning starts from the products and then works out the activities.

  • AActivity-based
  • BException-based
  • CProduct-based
  • DCost-based
Show the answer

Answer: C. Product-based planning starts from products.

S4Which management product hands work from the project manager to a team manager?

  • AHighlight report
  • BRisk register
  • CWork package description
  • DIssue report
Show the answer

Answer: C. The work package description defines the work and the product.

S5Why is only the next stage planned in detail?

  • ABecause later stages are not needed
  • BBecause the board does not want plans
  • CBecause the planning horizon limits how far ahead plans can be reliable
  • DBecause stage plans are optional
Show the answer

Answer: C. Detail is reliable only near; later stages are in outline.

S6Which describes a dependency?

  • AAn item or activity that must happen before another can start or finish
  • BA written report to the board
  • CA type of quality test
  • DA type of risk response
Show the answer

Answer: A. That is a dependency.

5.2 Recall questions

R1Name the four plan levels.

Show the answer

Project plan, stage plan, team plan and exception plan.

R2What triggers an exception plan?

Show the answer

A tolerance forecast to be exceeded.

R3What is the first step of product-based planning?

Show the answer

Write the project product description.

R4What is a work package description?

Show the answer

The work to be done and the product to deliver, given to a team manager.

R5Define scope.

Show the answer

The sum of the work (products and activities) to be done.

R6What is a planning horizon?

Show the answer

How far ahead you can plan reliably.

6Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
Plan levels project, stage, team, exception
Product-based planning project product description, PBS, product descriptions, flow diagram
Tolerances permissible deviation before escalation
Products project product description, work package description, plan
